$comment: SPDX-License-Identifier: MPL-2.0. Meguri-owned protocol between Meguri tooling and oracle workers.
title: Meguri oracle worker protocol, version 1
description: A worker is one long-lived process serving exactly one time zone (its TZ) with a frozen clock that only scenarios move. Transport: one JSON request per line on stdin, one JSON response per line on stdout, in request order; no ports. A failed request gets ok=false and the worker keeps serving. Start a worker with `tools/mg oracle build`, whose result.json gives the image as details.image.tag (meguri-oracle:<tag>), then `MEGURI_ORACLE_TAG=<tag> docker compose -f docker/compose.yml run --rm -T --no-deps -e TZ=<zone> oracle`. A checkout without oracle/ (an implementer worktree) works the same way: tools/mg builds the image from the main worktree's oracle/, and the run needs only the built image. Goldens written by `tools/mg oracle record` are {scenario_id, scenario_sha256, oracle: {anki_version, lock_sha256, driver_sha256}, tz, clock: {start, mode}, observations}, sorted keys, LF, one file per scenario at the scenario's relative path with a .json suffix; scenario_sha256 is the lower-case hex sha256 of the RFC 8785 (JCS) text of the parsed scenario value (YAML read with the 1.2 core schema), so comments, key order and layout never change it. golden.schema.json and scenario.schema.json (U4) are authoritative for those formats.

id.description: Optional correlation value, echoed unchanged in the response.

run_request.description: Batch mode: run one scenario on a fresh collection and return every step's output; a handoff step only closes and reopens the collection there. With steps, resume or handoff it runs one segment of a live chain (dsl.md D9.2) instead: needs a worker started with ORACLE_HANDOFF (the handoff directory it shares with the runner).

steps.description: [first, end): run only these scenario steps; observations.steps then holds their outputs, and error.step stays the scenario's step index.

resume.description: Start from this handoff instead of a fresh collection and the setup.

handoff.description: After the last step, close the collection, copy the session directory to this directory (relative to ORACLE_HANDOFF; it must not exist) and return state.

begin_request.description: Interactive mode: set up the scenario (clock, collection, setup) without running its steps.

step_request.description: Interactive mode: without step, run the scenario's next step (no_more_steps after the last; a failed step stays next); with step, run that ad-hoc step, which does not move the scenario's next step.

end_request.description: Interactive mode: close and delete the session's collection and return the outputs of the steps run.

lock_sha256.description: sha256 of oracle/requirements.lock, which pins the per-architecture wheel hashes.

driver_sha256.description: sha256 over the driver's source files (tests excluded).

elapsed_ms.description: Wall time inside the worker; never part of a golden.

state.description: Present when the request asked for a handoff.

handoff_state.description: What crosses a handoff (dsl.md D9.2): the session directory (collection.anki2, its media, files ops wrote) at dir, relative to the handoff directory; the clock in epoch seconds; the real ids behind #n1, #n2... and #c1, #c2... in order.

steps.description: Number of steps in the scenario.

index.description: The step's position in the output that end returns, ad-hoc steps included; a failed step request reports the same position as error.step.

error.description: Driver-authored fields only: never Anki's (localized) message text.

kind.description: unsupported_op/_observation/_setup: the driver has no such op, observation or setup section (the scenario needs a newer driver); protocol_error: the line is not a JSON request (NaN and Infinity are not JSON), or a run request's segment fields are malformed; anki_error: Anki raised outside an op's rejection kinds (exception names its class; a refusal in the op's list is an output, dsl.md D7.3); handoff_error: no ORACLE_HANDOFF, or a handoff directory that is missing, already there or outside it; internal_error: a driver bug, including a response JSON cannot carry (then id is echoed only if it can be).

detail.description: Driver-authored English, for people; never compare it.

observations.description: One output per scenario step, in step order, so /steps/<i>/... points into step i.

step_output.description: An op step: {}, {<op>: <result>}, or {<op>: {"error": <kind>}} when Anki refused it with one of the op's rejection kinds (dsl.md D7.3; the run goes on). An observe step: {<kind>: <value>} per requested kind; per-card kinds are keyed by logical id (#c1, #n1). f32 values are the shortest decimal that parses back to the same f32.

scenario.description: Driver vocabulary v0; scenario.schema.json (U4) is authoritative for the file format. Logical ids: notes #n1, #n2... and cards #c1, #c2... in creation order (a note's cards in template order). Setup sections run in this order: config, presets, decks, notetypes, notes.

compare.description: Comparison hints for the runner; the driver ignores them.

tz.description: IANA zone; must equal the worker's zone.

start.description: ISO 8601 date-time in whole seconds: wall time in tz, or with an offset. A wall time inside a DST gap is invalid; a repeated one means its first occurrence.

mode.description: Recorded in the golden. The clock is frozen in both; it moves only through advance and set_clock.

config.description: Collection config keys and JSON values (e.g. fsrs, loadBalancerEnabled, rollover), written in sorted key order.

presets.description: Deck option presets. A preset named Default edits the default preset. Options: learn_steps, relearn_steps (durations), graduating_interval_days, easy_interval_days, new_per_day, reviews_per_day, max_interval_days, min_lapse_interval_days, starting_ease, easy_bonus, hard_interval, interval_modifier, lapse_new_interval, leech_threshold, leech_action (suspend|tag_only), bury_new, bury_reviews, bury_interday_learning, desired_retention, fsrs_params.

notetypes.description: {name, kind?: standard|cloze, fields: [names], templates: [{name, front, back}], css?}. Scenarios define their own note types and CSS.

notes.description: {notetype, deck?, fields: [string] | {field: string}, tags?: [string]}, as add_note. Field values and tags are strings: quote numbers, booleans and null.

step.description: One key. Ops v0: advance <duration: 20m, 1d, 23h40m; a day is 86400 s>; set_clock <date-time as clock.start>; add_note <note, as setup.notes; output {note, cards}>; answer {card, rating: again|hard|good|easy, time_ms?}; handoff <meguri|oracle> (live scenarios; in a whole run it closes and reopens the collection). observe [<kind> | '<kind>(#ref, ...)' | {<kind>: args}]: ids, timing {days_elapsed, next_day_at, now, utc_offset_secs}, card (cards row: nid as #nN, did/odid as deck names, data parsed), revlog (rows by id, cid as #cN), next_states ({current, again, hard, good, easy}: {kind, ...fields, memory_state?}), fuzz_table {card, pairs: [[card_id, reps]], intervals} -> {intervals, rows: [[card_id, reps, delta...]]} (fuzz when answering a card with that id and review count), net_probe {host, port, timeout_ms?} -> {connected, error}.
